text:
maya: Quick sync — need to finalize SLOs + launch acceptance for the Inference Resilience PRD. Can we lock latency/error budgets and graceful-degrade modes? cc @sam @nina @raj

sam: On it. Draft proposal below, open to pushback.
```
SLOs (hosted default):
- first-token p50 <= 40ms
- first-token p95 <= 200ms
- end-to-end (long seqs) p95 <= 700ms
- error-rate (5xx/timeout) <= 0.6% per 1h window
```

nina: p95 200ms is tight for multi-tenant during noisy neighbor spikes. Dedicated customers should get tighter SLAs, yes. For hosted we should pair with auto-burst fallback to smaller model.

raj: Important question — are fallbacks allowed to change output shape/semantics (e.g., shorter summaries or different tokenization)? Customers will notice.

maya: We should allow semantic-preserving fallbacks only. Acceptance criteria idea: mean semantic-diff <= 2% across the eval prompt set when in degrade mode (we can operationalize with the eval harness). Also require an explicit customer-visible notice in the response metadata when degradations happen.

leo: Ops notes: error-budget burn policy suggestion:
- warn (Slack + monitoring): 50% of budget burned in last 1h
- action: scale + fallback at 70% burn in 30m
- page oncall at 90% burn in 15m
This keeps auto-remediation in front of paging.

sam: Also propose a circuit-breaker that switches to latency-first model variant when first-token p95 > 300ms for 5m continuously. It should be reversible and tested in canary.

nina: Edge-case we need to call out: streaming requests where partial responses are delivered. Which metric counts? My vote: first-token latency for SLOs, and a separate completeness metric (end-to-end) tracked for quality regressions.

raj: For the PRD, please include these acceptance tests:
- eval harness diff threshold and test vectors
- smoke tests for canary (latency + correctness)
- rollout plan: dark launch -> canary -> gradual -> full with automatic rollback on SLO breach

maya: Will add those to PRD. Timeline: aiming PRD ready by Fri EOD, spec review on Tue next week. Can the runtime + SRE teams sign off on numbers by Tue? :eyes:

leo: Ops + runtime + SRE will triage. Proposed sync Thurs 10am PT to finalize operational runbook. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued: "resilience-loadtest/canary-42" — logs: https://ci.redwood.example/resilience-loadtest/canary-42 (will post results here).

maya: thanks — once canary results in we can iterate numbers quickly.

sam: quick nit: add an acceptance criterion for token-cost delta when falling back (must be documented and within expected cost band).

nina: +1. also flag customer comms template (how we notify about degraded mode) as part of launch checklist.

maya: Good call. I'll add: comms template, eval harness link, canary checklist, and runbook. Locking on numbers by Tue unless major objections.

raj: acked. If anyone sees an unresolvable tradeoff, drop it here and we'll escalate to PM sync.

leo: ack. Meeting invite sent for Thurs 10am PT.

maya: closing thread for now — will push PRD updates later today. :rocket:
